items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Sergio went to Viareggio every year... So if he could arrange for us to go to the casino... we engaged an Italian bass man and rehearsed at Sangiorgi's home until the time came for us to go to Viareggio.

ctx.x: The 31st of May, I finished at the Florida club. Meantime,

Count Sergio Sangiorgi had contacted the owner of a casino in Viareggio, Italy and this man came to Rome in June to talk over the prospects of engaging a band for his place and the deal came through. Sergio went to Viareggio every year for his summer vacation, and he was sweet on Astrella also. So if he could arrange for us to go to the casino, he was certain to have some jazz when he wanted to hear it in person and be with Arstella. "Bass" Hill had been contacted quite a while back for a job somewhere in Germany…

From the time that I had finished at the Florida Club until I went to Viareggio, I didn't have one gig. Lily could speak Italian and one day, when she was in the kitchen, the woman that we rented from, asked her why I did not try to get a job, perhaps as a dishwasher in some restaurant. Lily tried to explain to her that there are times when artist in music and show business had periods when there was no work and don't favour washing dishes or doing other kind of work that is not to their liking.
